definition: EX/RP refers to exposure and response prevention, a cognitive-behavioral treatment approach for obsessive–compulsive disorder in which patients confront feared situations or thoughts while refraining from their usual compulsive responses. In this packet, adherence to EX/RP during and between sessions was measured as an indicator of treatment engagement.

reasons: The packet supports EX/RP only as part of the name of the Patient Exposure and Response Prevention (EX/RP) Adherence Scale (PEAS), not as the term for the treatment itself.

The statement that EX/RP is a cognitive-behavioral treatment approach for obsessive–compulsive disorder is not directly supported by the packet; the packet mentions ERP as the CBT focus, but not EX/RP in that sense.
The claim that patients confront feared situations or thoughts while refraining from compulsive responses is not stated in the packet.

The sentence about adherence to EX/RP during and between sessions being measured as an indicator of treatment engagement is only partly supported; the packet says in- and between-session patient adherence was measured with PEAS and may reflect treatment engagement, but it does not state this as a general definition of EX/RP.

The packet only states that CBT “focuses on exposure and response prevention (ERP)” as the primary psychological treatment for OCD, but it does not support the additional description that patients “confront feared situations or thoughts” while “refraining from their usual compulsive responses.”

The definition’s wording frames EX/RP as a specific “cognitive-behavioral treatment approach” and includes behavioral targets not explicitly described in the provided packet text beyond the general ERP focus.
